notes: Fifteen lists read. oecd.org returned 403 (also the Better Life Index redirect) and web.archive.org is blocked, so OECD entries are the Work-life balance indicators, with definitions quoted from a Sustainable Brands summary of the OECD index; the gender gap indicator has no passage. The WHOQOL-BREF PDFs loaded but their text could not be extracted, so Q14 has no passage. Gallup Most Important Problem, Ipsos What Worries the World and the WHO/IHME cause-of-burden lists name no time, chores, paperwork, legal or screen-time pain, so they have no entries here. Wikidata QIDs came from the wbsearchentities API (rate-limited; about 20 lookups, not counted as searches). Candidates: no-time-off sits close to the Work group; benefits-runaround overlaps life-admin (Paperwork) and legal-mess. Life-admin has no Wikidata item in the catalog; Q116039772 (paperwork) fits. The rushed and time-crunch figures are old (Pew 2005, Gallup 2015); no newer U.S. series was found. Leads not proposed because no opened list names them: unpredictable shift schedules, waiting on hold, boredom or empty time. Withdrawn at the coordinator's request because the work sweep 20261019-224658 covers them: long-commute (same ID there) and sick-days (near-duplicate of no-paid-leave). Their entries are recorded out of scope. Sources kept: long-commute: https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021/one-way-travel-time-to-work-rises.html ("the average one-way commute in the United States increased to a new high of 27.6 minutes in 2019"); long-commute: https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021/one-way-travel-time-to-work-rises.html ("the percentage of workers reporting commutes of 60 minutes or longer increased from 7.9% in 2006 to 9.8% in 2019"); sick-days: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ebs2.nr0.htm ("81 percent had access to paid sick leave"); sick-days: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ebs2.nr0.htm ("Access to paid sick leave for private industry workers ranged from 58 percent for the leisure and hospitality industry").
